# reportControls/

The controls that decide what a report surface SHOWS. Nothing here changes
what a figure IS — every number still comes from a service and is copied, not
derived. That line is the whole point of the directory: a toggle that also
changed an amount would make two screens disagree about the same period.

## Caller contract

- `<ComparatorControls value onChange comparators? />` — one checkbox per field
  on `StatementColumns`. `comparators` names the ones this surface can supply
  (default both). The balance sheet passes `['prior']`: budgets are P&L
  figures and their account codes match nothing on a balance sheet, so a
  Budget column there would print empty cells that read as missing data.
- `useComparatorColumns()` → `{ columns, setColumns }`. Seeds from the density
  ONCE it has resolved and never after the user has touched a checkbox — the
  server preference lands on a later tick and re-seeding then would undo a
  column the user had just switched on.
- `useStatementComparators({ trend, budget, asOf, basis, periodStart, periodEnd })`
  → `{ apply, budgetState, trendFailed, trendLoading, budgetLoading }`.
  `apply` decorates `StatementRow[]`. `budgetState` is
  `unknown | failed | none | available` — `failed` must never be shown as
  `none`. The two loading flags are per fetch; one shared flag would report
  the budget as loaded because the trend finished.
- `<ComparatorNotices budgetState trendFailed />` and the pure
  `comparatorNotices(...)` behind it — what the columns could not tell you.
- `useDensity()` → `{ density, setDensity, loading, error }` /
  `<DensityToggle density onChange />` — `owner` | `accountant`, persisted to
  `reports_density` on `/api/auth/preferences` and mirrored into
  `isaflow_reports_density` for the first paint. `error` is set when the SAVE
  is rejected.

## Business rules

- **Variance needs something to vary against.** Turning off the last
  comparator turns Variance off too; the box is disabled while none is on.
  Four empty cells per row read as a broken report, not as an off switch.
- **The trend column is independent of any comparator** — it is the account's
  own twelve months, not a comparison.
- **The trend and the budget are COMPANY-WIDE, and a selected cost centre
  withholds them.** `trendRowsService` applies no cost-centre filter and
  `getBudgetVariance` takes no cost centre, while both statement pages do pass
  `cost_centre_id` to the statement fetch. Drawn together, a company-wide
  sparkline sits in the same row as a departmental figure. With a cost centre
  selected both checkboxes are disabled (`companyWideUnavailable`), the
  comparators are NOT fetched, and `ComparatorNotices` says why. The reader's
  own checkbox state is kept untouched so clearing the filter restores it.
- **`basis` is not a preference.** `movement` for P&L accounts, `balance` for
  balance-sheet accounts. The wrong one draws a shape about a different number
  than the one printed beside it.
- **A zero prior keeps its movement.** Nothing to R5.5m is a movement of
  R5.5m and is printed. Only `variancePct` is dropped — no denominator, and
  the services' 0 placeholder would print as "0.0%" beside the largest
  movement on the statement. `baseComparison` in `statementRows/comparators.ts`.
- **Retained earnings gets no trend.** `trendRowsService` returns it in
  `unavailable` and `applyTrend` leaves `trend` undefined, so the grid prints
  an empty cell rather than a line flat at zero beside a figure in the
  millions.
- **The comparators are fetched on the checkbox, not on page load.** Twelve
  months of movements plus a whole budget is a cost no user should pay for a
  column they never opened. Each effect CLEARS its state before refetching:
  the cancellation flag stops an out-of-order write but does not blank what is
  already on screen, so without it the previous window's sparklines sit beside
  the new window's figures.
- **A failed fetch is not an empty column.** An empty trend cell already means
  "this account has no series" and an empty budget column already means "no
  budget was captured". Rendering a network failure as either states something
  about the ledger that nobody checked, so both are named in
  `ComparatorNotices`.
- **"Is there a budget" comes from the service, not from the amounts.** The
  route returns `budgetedCount` (`result.rows.length`). Inferring it from
  all-zero amounts cannot tell "no budget captured" from "budgeted at zero on
  every line".
- **`apiFetch` resolves on 4xx.** Every request in this directory goes through
  `assertOk` or `apiJson`; a bare `.catch` would only ever see a dropped
  connection, and a rejected save would look identical to a successful one.

## Files
- `ComparatorControls.tsx` — the four checkboxes.
- `useComparatorColumns.ts` — density-seeded column state. `DENSITY_COLUMNS`
  is the seed table.
- `useStatementComparators.ts` — the two fetches and `apply`.
- `ComparatorNotices.tsx` — the sentences for a missing or unloadable
  comparator. `comparatorNotices` is exported and pure.
- `useDensity.ts`, `DensityToggle.tsx` — the reading-density preference.
